note: Issue #108/#192 costmap-silhouette capture. Live `openral deploy sim` graph (slam + nav2 + octomap, reasoner on, no policy dispatched) on q-laptop / RTX 5070 Laptop, ROS 2 Jazzy, RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp. One graph launch per scene, each at its pinned seed. Nav2 driven by a single direct NavigateToPose goal 2.0 m ahead in `map`, so the base translates and both rolling windows sweep new geometry. Produced by `tools/_nav2_costmap_silhouette_probe.py`: every cell centre of every published Costmap is transformed into base_link and tested against the manifest's bare chassis polygon (`base_footprint_polygon`) plus any attached primitives, using `payload_scan_filter_node`'s own containment predicates. Re-run 2026-09-05 after code review tightened the tool: `verdict` and the exit code now honour the non-vacuity guards, so a costmap that marked nothing anywhere reports VACUOUS instead of clean. `total_marked_in_silhouette` counts cells at exactly LETHAL_OBSTACLE (254) - not 253, which is what an inflation layer writes near a legitimate obstacle somewhere else.

finding: The GLOBAL costmap is EMPTY on both scenes: max cost 0 over 50 and 52 published samples, zero non-zero cells at any point, while the LOCAL costmap on the same graph peaks at 254 with 1982 / 1050 non-zero cells. Its `obstacle_layer` is configured on the same filtered `/openral/nav2/scan` the local costmap's `voxel_layer` reads, `static_layer` is deliberately out of its plugin chain (rolling window, SLAM-from-scratch), and `planner_server` logs no warning of any kind. NavfnPlanner therefore planned the accepted NavigateToPose goal against a blank 20x20 m grid. Not what #192 set out to measure, not fixed here, and it makes the GLOBAL half of the silhouette verdict VACUOUS - nothing is marked inside the robot because nothing is marked at all. The LOCAL half is non-vacuous and is the result this file records.

root_cause: The global costmap's emptiness is the HEIGHT FILTER, not the topic and not TF. Measured on a live graph: global_costmap IS subscribed to /openral/nav2/scan with matching BEST_EFFORT QoS (3 subscribers: local_costmap, collision_monitor, global_costmap), and 97 of 102 scans transform into `map` at their own stamps (map<-odom is 0.35-0.50 s AHEAD of each scan stamp; /tf runs at 62 Hz). But nav2's ObservationBuffer applies min_obstacle_height / max_obstacle_height in the costmap's OWN global frame, and the two costmaps do not share one. TF measured: odom->base_link z=+0.700, odom->base_scan z=+0.300, map->odom z=-0.700 (slam_toolbox flattens base_link to z=0 in map), map->base_scan z=-0.400. Both costmaps ship min_obstacle_height: 0.0 - so in `odom` the returns are at +0.30 m and are kept, and in `map` they are at -0.40 m and every one is discarded before it can mark.

caveat: Two attribution limits, stated so the numbers are not over-read. (1) `openral_sim.backends.robocasa.synthesize_laser_scan_2d` re-casts through the robot's own MuJoCo kinematic tree, so a self-return never enters /scan in sim in the first place. A clean silhouette here is the END STATE being correct; it is not proof that payload_scan_filter_node is what made it so. That attribution is what the deterministic sweep in tests/integration/test_nav2_scan_filter_live.py exists for - it ships a control that fails. (2) attached_objects stayed 0 on both runs (no policy was dispatched, so nothing was ever grasped), so the PAYLOAD half of the silhouette is unmeasured and is reported as payload_silhouette_measured: false rather than as a clean verdict.

self_mark_permanence: Separate finding, from making the live-lane sweep deterministic after it failed in CI. A self-return that reaches the cost grid ONCE is permanent. The scan filter fails open by design (a scan it cannot place is republished untouched - the more-obstacles direction), but it then removes exactly the beam whose ray would have cleared the cell it let through. Measured on a real nav2_costmap_2d with this package's topic wiring: phase 1, unfiltered ring at 0.20 m -> 32 cells marked inside the chassis; phase 2, filtered ring with every self beam = inf, 20 s -> still 32; phase 3, real returns at 3.0 m on the same bearings -> 0. Phase 3 is the control: Nav2's clearing works, there simply has to BE a ray. collision_monitor reads the same topic and has no costmap-side clearing at all. The obvious fix (write range_max instead of inf so the beam raytrace-clears) is NOT obviously safe - it turns the filter from 'leave the map alone' into 'erase 3 m along this bearing', so a beam dropped in error would delete a real obstacle. Recorded, not changed.

reproduction: Both scenes re-run in an independent session before merge, whole graph relaunched per scene. The conclusion reproduces and the incidental counts do not, which is what a live scene run looks like: local costmap ZERO LETHAL cells inside a 140 / 141-cell silhouette on baguette / deliver_straw, in samples carrying 127 / 59 marked cells elsewhere, base driven 0.954 / 1.318 m; global costmap max cost 0 on both, so the tool reports VACUOUS for the global half and exits non-zero. The two records that follow are that run's raw output. Recorded because this corpus's standing caveat is that its only two completions were never reproduced.

self_mark_permanence_resolution: 2026-09-05, issue #212 closed by fix/212-self-mark-permanence. The permanence itself is NOT undone -- the fail-open window that creates it is closed instead. `payload_scan_filter_node` now publishes NOTHING while a self-polygon is configured and `base_frame <- scan_frame` has never resolved, bounded by the new `self_tf_grace_s` param (default 5.0 s), after which it reverts to pass-through and logs an error -- a permanently blind Nav2 (mistyped `base_frame`) is the worse of the two failures. The gate arms once; a TF gap after the first successful resolve still fails open, which is the one-scan-at-a-time case the payload half's reasoning already covers. Verified against the pre-fix node: the same test observed 58 unfiltered scans published in the 4 s window and now observes 0.
rejected_option: Option 1 of #212 (publish `range_max` for a chassis-dropped beam so Nav2 raytraces it clear) is REJECTED on a measurement, not a preference. Its justification -- the endpoint is provably inside the manifest polygon, so nothing real is erased -- covers the wrong segment: Nav2 clears the ray out to `raytrace_max_range` (3.0 m in `config/nav2_panda_mobile.yaml`), an order of magnitude past the chassis, and a bearing on which the chassis returns is one the sensor is PERMANENTLY occluded on, so the erased cells were marked from other robot poses and nothing on that bearing re-marks them. Measured live on `nav2_costmap_2d` (Jazzy binary) with this package's wiring: a real obstacle at 0.60 m on the forward bearings, cost 254, goes to cost 0 when one beam carrying `range_max - 1e-4` (12.0 - 0.0001 m; nav2's own inf-substitution epsilon, and `laser_geometry`'s cutoff is a strict `<`) is published on the same bearing. Pinned as `test_raytrace_clearing_a_dropped_beam_would_erase_a_real_obstacle` in `tests/integration/test_nav2_scan_filter_live.py`.
residual: A mark that does land inside the chassis is freed by nav2's `footprint_clearing_enabled` (default True, not overridden in the shipped config); the phase 1/2/3 table above turns it off so the filter is what is measured. It frees cells whose CENTRE falls inside the published polygon (`setConvexPolygonCost`), so a cell straddling the boundary is not reached -- a band under one 0.05 m cell wide, reachable only through the bounded grace fallback. Not separately mitigated.

global_costmap_emptiness_resolution: FIXED 2026-09-05 (#211, PR pending). The height gate is turned OFF on the global costmap rather than retuned: obstacle_layer min/max_obstacle_height = -10.0 / +10.0 at BOTH the layer level and the scan-source level. /openral/nav2/scan is a planar LaserScan and obstacle_layer is a 2-D layer, so every point shares one z and the gate can only admit all or none - it has no discriminating power to lose. +/-10 m is past anything a frame in this stack can offset that plane by (the largest is the 0.700 m pedestal), so the window is inert rather than tuned and cannot go wrong again when a frame's floor moves.
two_gates: MEASURED, not inferred from the source. nav2 applies the height cut TWICE from two differently-scoped parameters of the same name: ObservationBuffer::bufferCloud uses obstacle_layer.scan.min/max_obstacle_height (defaults 0.0 / 0.0) at buffer time after the transform into global_frame, and ObstacleLayer::updateBounds uses the LAYER-level obstacle_layer.min/max_obstacle_height (defaults 0.0 / 2.0) again per point while marking. With the layer-level pair removed and the source pair at +/-10 m the global costmap is STILL empty - widening only the source pair fixes nothing.
rejected_options: Option 2 (stop slam_toolbox injecting z into map->odom) rewrites a frame contract the octomap bridge and the kernel's voxel grid (ADR-0095) also read, to fix a filter that should not have been filtering. Moving base_link to ground level contradicts ADR-0095, which makes it the arm mount deliberately. Copying this window to the LOCAL costmap would be wrong: that layer is a VoxelLayer with a real z column (origin_z 0.0, 16 x 0.08 m) where the height bounds do carry meaning.
evidence: tests/integration/test_nav2_global_costmap_height_live.py, on the live lane. A real nav2_costmap_2d reads the SHIPPED config/nav2_panda_mobile.yaml off disk under the measured map->odom->base_link->base_scan chain (-0.700 / +0.700 / -0.400) and marks a 1 m obstacle at cost 254; the paired control restores the pre-fix gate and asserts the grid goes empty. Negative control run: with the pre-fix config restored the first test fails with 'the global costmap marked nothing anywhere'.
still_vacuous: DISCHARGED 2026-09-05. The probe was re-run on both scenes after the fix - see the recapture note and the two scene records that follow. The global costmap is now non_vacuous: true on both, so the global half of #207's costmap-clean verdict measures something for the first time. The PAYLOAD half is still unmeasured on scenes: attached_objects stayed 0 on every run because no policy was dispatched, so nothing was ever grasped. That is #108's own remaining gate, untouched by #211.

what_this_settles: Issue #211's stated acceptance: global_costmap.max_cost_seen > 0 and nonzero_cells_max > 0 on both scenes. And the second item: LETHAL cells inside the robot silhouette stay at 0 - now NON-vacuously, since the same samples carry 164 and 254 marked cells elsewhere against a ~136-138 cell chassis silhouette. Three baguette/straw runs, three clean verdicts.
what_it_does_not_settle: attached_objects_seen is 0 on every run and payload_silhouette_measured is false, because no policy was dispatched and nothing was grasped. The payload half of the silhouette is still measured only on the deterministic rig. Unchanged by #211; it is #108's gate.

payload_half_on_a_scene: 2026-09-05. The PAYLOAD half of the silhouette sweep, measured on a real scene for the first time. Method: scenes/deploy/robocasa_baguette.yaml at seed 1 with runtime enable_reasoner=false and the XR-1 robocasa365 policy dispatched directly at /openral/execute_rskill (tools/_validation_matrix_dispatch.py), i.e. the same direct-dispatch stack tools/validation_matrix.py has run since 2026-08-13. The S2 reasoner is off because it requires OPENRAL_REASONER_API_KEY; the S1 policy that grasps is real. The probe is started BEFORE the dispatch and spins through the whole episode, because the attach window on this scene runs 5-15 s and a probe started ON the attach spends most of it in its own rclpy/TF startup. A separate drive_on_attach helper sends one NavigateToPose 2 m ahead the moment the payload attaches, so base travel and payload attachment overlap.
blocker_found_and_fixed: payload_silhouette_measured could NEVER become true on a scene. tools/_nav2_costmap_silhouette_probe.py incremented its `placed` count once per successfully-placed PRIMITIVE and compared it against `declared` = the number of OBJECTS. Sim payloads come from extract_body_primitives over a MuJoCo body subtree and carry many: /openral/attachment_state on this carry records n_primitives=16 for the single sim:obj_main object. So placed=16 vs declared=1 filed every sample as a partial placement. The guard was unsatisfiable, not unsatisfied - which is why every scene run in this file reports the payload half unmeasured. Now counted per object, with an object placed only when every one of its primitives projected. Regression test: tests/unit/test_nav2_costmap_probe_payload_count.py (registered in scripts/ros_live_tests.sh); reverting the count makes 2 of its 4 tests fail.
result: MEASURED and CLEAN. Runs 13, 15 and 17: payload_silhouette_measured true on BOTH costmaps, payload_partial_samples 0, total_marked_in_silhouette 0, non_vacuous true, base_travel 0.523 / 0.601 / 0.748 m. Run 16 was measured and clean but travelled 0.097 m, just under the 0.10 m floor, so it self-reports VACUOUS on travel and is not counted.
one_marked_verdict_adjudicated: Run 14 returned MARKED CELLS INSIDE SILHOUETTE - 2 cells global, 4 local - and it is a PROBE FALSE POSITIVE, not a scan-filter failure. Every flagged cell sat at x = 0.39-0.44 m in base_link, i.e. 4-9 cm PAST the 0.35 m chassis edge and therefore under the payload's projection rather than the chassis's. But both costmaps' only observation source is the planar scan, and the payload cannot reach that plane: measured on the same runs, the payload sits at z = 1.43 m in odom against a 0.30 m scan plane (probe-reported span in base_link: 0.188 to 0.348, i.e. 0.59-0.75 m above the plane). A carried object that clears the lidar by 0.6 m cannot have marked those cells; they are the counter the robot was parked at, seen at scan height, lying beneath the payload's vertical projection. Run 7 flagged the same 0.41-0.46 m band. The probe now records payload_z_span_in_base_m in every verdict so this is adjudicable from the artifact instead of being read as the filter failing.
what_is_still_not_measured: A COMPLETED task. Every run E-stopped or dropped the payload before the place phase: the grasp held 5-15 s, the goals ended safety_estop (kind_collision (world) / kind_controller (n_dof)), and none placed the baguette in the cabinet. The measurement here is the costmap silhouette DURING a real carry with the base driving, which is what #108's payload half asks for; it is not a task-success claim and must not be quoted as one. docs/reference/collision-validation-evidence.md records 2/5 completions on this scene, so the E-stops are the known open collision-stack work, not a new finding.
harness_faults_to_not_repeat: Two of the 17 attempts were lost to the harness, not the robot. (1) Repeated launch/kill cycles on ROS_DOMAIN_ID 0 exhausted Cyclone's participant table - 'Failed to find a free participant index for domain 0' - so the dispatcher could not create a node and the round read as 'never grasped'. Each attempt now gets its own domain. (2) A killed run left an XR-1 sidecar holding 3.6 GB of an 8 GB card, starving the next attempt; teardown now kills orphaned GPU compute processes.

estop_investigation: 2026-09-05. Why every carry run E-stopped or dropped the payload before the place phase. Three distinct causes, only one of them a product defect.
cause_1_harness_dds_crosstalk: kind_controller (n_dof) in the two earliest runs: NOT a product fault. The kernel logged safety.envelope_violation kind=controller field=n_dof value=1 and value=2 against limit=11, one of them carrying rskill_id=place_in_cabinet - a string that exists nowhere in the repo except cpp/openral_safety_kernel/test/test_lifecycle_kernel.cpp, which publishes deliberately malformed chunks to prove the kernel rejects them. On the shared ROS_DOMAIN_ID 0 those reached the deploy graph's kernel, which correctly rejected them and latched an E-stop. Zero n_dof violations once each attempt got its own domain. Confirmed independently by recording every chunk on /openral/candidate_action for a whole run: XR-1 slot-dispatches CARTESIAN_DELTA n_dof=6, GRIPPER_POSITION n_dof=1, JOINT_VELOCITY n_dof=11 and COMPOSITE_MODE n_dof=1, and none of them can trip the joint-mode equality check.
cause_2_a_real_collision: Run 13 is a legitimate stop. Ground truth: robot0_link6 vs cab_1_left_group_right_door_g2 at -0.010770 m, distance_certified true, method sat, and MuJoCo reports the contact in robot_world_contacts. The arm is 10.8 mm inside the cabinet door. The kernel was right.
cause_3_the_defect_the_voxel_backing_lie: All three world-collision stops (runs 13, 15, 16) report evidence_voxel_backing verdict 'unbacked' with rays_cast=27 and rays_hit=0 - 'a phantom or stale cell'. They are not phantom cells; the probe looked in the wrong place. SimSensorBridge._late_voxel_backing called voxel_backing_record WITHOUT grid_orientation_xyzw and so took the identity default, while the in-snapshot caller passed it. The published lattice is the OctoMap's, so on a rotated base the decoded cube lands elsewhere: the three cells decoded to world positions 2.9-3.1 m from the stopping link, which cannot be 5-33 mm inside a panda link or a payload in the gripper. That is the confident-verdict-about-the-wrong-cube failure voxel_backing_record's own contract forbids, and it is on the path that matters - the snapshot is never delayed for the kernel's evidence, so the late path adjudicated 14 of 15 stops across the 2026-08-26 battery and 3 of 3 here. Fixed by voxel_backing_for_cell, the one place a cell dict is unpacked. Any past round that called a world-voxel stop a phantom on the strength of a LATE backing record needs re-reading.
cause_4_the_payload_drop: Run 16 shows the sequence: t+0.00 attachment revision 1 sim:obj_main; t+0.03 support_witness_armed object=sim:obj_main support=sim:counter_1_left_group_main; t+0.09 the octomap bridge clears 47 cells for the payload but WITHHOLDS 1 attested support patch; t+1.08 the attachment perception barrier releases; t+3.23 safety.collision a=attached:sim:obj_main b=voxel_239470 min_distance_m=-0.026095; t+5.49 attachment revision 2 (released). XR-1 closes on the baguette while it is still resting on the counter and does not lift promptly, so the payload sits in the withheld support-patch voxels of its own support surface. Ground truth agrees the contact is real but small: payload vs counter -0.002583 m certified. The stop is conservative and defensible; whether a grasped-but-unlifted payload should be exempt is a safety-WG question (it would make the kernel LESS conservative), not a patch. Recorded, not changed.
